Four 'extraordinary' Renaissance paintings stolen from Italian museum
- Published
Four Renaissance paintings of "extraordinary value" have been stolen from a museum in Sicily, Italy's culture minister has said.
Alessandro Giuli confirmed that three panels of the Polyptych of San Gregorio and a double-sided panel of the Madonna with Child and Christ in Pietà, all attributed to Antonello da Messina, were taken from the Regional Interdisciplinary Museum of Messina on Saturday night.
Police are now probing how the thieves were able to enter the museum without triggering its alarms and who may have been responsible.
The incident is the latest in a string of museum heists across Europe that have led to a growing number of priceless works disappearing from public view.
Investigators are working on the initial suspicion that the paintings were stolen to order by black market art thieves, according to Italian news agency Ansa.
It reported that the Madonna and Christ in Pietà was removed directly from inside a secure display case, while all the paintings taken were on wooden panels, preventing them from easily being rolled up.
The museum's director Marisa Mercurio said the theft was thought to have occurred around 21:50 local time (19:50 GMT) on Saturday.
"We are shocked by what happened," she told Ansa, describing it as "a great loss for the museum, for the city, the community and the art world".
Antonello da Messina was a 15th Century painter born and raised on Sicily, who would go on to become one of the early Renaissance period's master painters.
His San Gregorio Polyptych, painted in 1473, depicts the Virgin Mary holding an infant Jesus Christ, flanked by St Gregory and St Benedict as well as several angels.
The artwork, of which five panels survive, was commissioned for the monastery of Santa Maria.
Meanwhile, his double-panel showing an infant Christ blessing a follower while being held by the Virgin Mary on one side and an adult Christ in death on the other was painted around the same time, though exactly when is unclear.
Its small size suggests it was originally used for private worship.
Federico Basile, the mayor of Messina, said he was "deeply outraged" by the "heinous criminal act".
"A heritage belonging to all the people of Messina has been violated," he said. "Messina will not let its history be stolen."
The theft comes just days after Italy's specialist art crime unit announced it had recovered three artworks stolen from a museum near Parma earlier this year.
The paintings by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse had a combined worth of €9m (£7.8m) and were taken by a gang in a matter of minutes, with the museum's alarm system preventing them from taking more.
The security of priceless artworks and artefacts in European museums was thrown into question late last year when a gang of thieves broke into the Louvre in Paris in broad daylight, making off with €88m worth of historic jewellery.

Father and five-year-old son found dead at Bengaluru home; police question wife
Police are questioning family members, including Abhinandan’s wife, as part of the probe.
A 35-year-old private company employee and his five-year-old son were found dead under suspicious circumstances at their residence in Gudde Basavapura, under Chikkabanavara police station limits in Karnataka's Bengaluru, on Monday morning.
The victims have been identified as Abhinandan, 35, a native of Kunigal, and his son Yaduveer, 5. Abhinandan was living at the house with his wife, Harini, and their son.
According to police, the incident came to light after Harini contacted the police helpline on Monday morning, reportedly telling them that the family had gone to a relative’s house and returned home on Sunday evening.
“When I woke up on Monday morning, I found my husband and son lying unresponsive,” Harini reportedly told the police.
Police personnel rushed to the house after receiving the call and found the father and son dead. Their bodies were taken into custody and sent for postmortem examination.
Senior police officers said there were no major external injuries on either of the bodies, though minor injury marks were noticed. The exact cause of death is expected to be established after the postmortem reports are received.
Police have also seized the mobile phones of both persons as part of the investigation. Officers are examining their call records, messages and other available digital evidence to establish the sequence of events before their deaths.
Deceased's mother alleges murder
The case took a serious turn after Abhinandan’s mother approached the police and lodged a complaint alleging that her son and grandson had been murdered. Based on the complaint and other suspicious circumstances noticed at the house, police registered a murder case and began a detailed investigation.
Bengaluru North-West Division DCP Nagesh D.L. said investigators had noticed several suspicious aspects at the residence.
“Based on the call received on the police helpline, Chikkabanavara police personnel went to the house and conducted an inspection. Some suspicious aspects were noticed at the spot. Abhinandan’s mother has filed a complaint alleging murder. Therefore, we have registered a murder case and are continuing the investigation,” the DCP said.
The police are also investigating the CCTV footage available at the house. Although CCTV cameras had been installed, officers found that the footage had not been properly saved.
“We are investigating whether the CCTV cameras were deliberately switched off or whether the footage was not saved for some other reason. This aspect is also part of our investigation,” Nagesh said.
Police are questioning family members, including Abhinandan’s wife, as part of the probe. Investigators are also examining whether any person entered or left the house around the time of the deaths.

Get your daily dose of health and medicine every weekday with STAT’s free newsletter Morning Rounds. Sign up here.
Good morning! Did you miss the newsletter last week? We’ve got a lot to catch up on, so let’s get right to it.
Everything the Trump administration did on health care last week
Last week was a busy one for federal health officials. On Monday, President Trump signed an executive order remaking the federal vaccine agenda, with little evidence to support the changes. The WHO criticized the move, and vaccine manufacturers indicated they would not fall in line. As a reminder: Here’s how we know that splitting up the MMR vaccine could be dangerous.
In the days after the announcement, health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. took a completely different tone while touring his MAHA message across California and avoiding more divisive issues like vaccines, as STAT’s Chelsea Cirruzzo reports today. Some more action from the week included:
- HHS announced that companies looking to add a new substance to human or animal foods will be required to notify the FDA and provide details on how they deemed the additive “generally recognized as safe.”
- CMS finalized a rule banning federal Medicaid and CHIP funds from covering gender-affirming care for minors. Legal challenges are inevitable, but experts told me that this restriction may be the Trump administration’s most legally viable move yet against these treatments. HHS also referred a large number of providers for investigation regarding gender-affirming care billing codes.
- The administration unveiled a new toolkit for battling addiction and homelessness that prioritized faith-based interventions while rejecting harm reduction principles. Released two years after methadone treatment regulations were modernized, the toolkit only passingly mentions the medication known to vastly reduce someone’s odds of dying from opioid overdose.
Private equity takeovers of doctor groups are stalling
Over a dozen states now have laws enhancing their oversight of private equity deals in health care. A new report says that’s slowing down dealmaking. In 2021, there were 851 physician practice management deals. But in the first half of 2026, there were just 105.
“Each of the state laws are different, and so it creates more uncertainty and just it’s a lot more work to figure out how a particular transaction triggers each of the state’s laws,” said Paul Pitts, a partner with Reed Smith who works with health care providers. STAT’s Tara Bannow has more.
Succession, lawsuits, and AI — oh my!
The situation unfolding at Epic, which sells the country’s dominant electronic health records software, sounds like something straight out of the HBO show “Succession.” The company is facing antitrust lawsuits and questions about its artificial intelligence strategy. And recently, there’s been an exodus of key technology leaders, including the presumed heir apparent to founder and CEO Judy Faulkner.
“You’ve got a lot of people who have been waiting their turn under an absolutely controlling leader,” said one former Epic employee who spent years at the company and remains in touch with former colleagues. “This was always going to be messy.” Ahead of Epic’s annual conference, beginning tomorrow, STAT’s Brittany Trang and Casey Ross dove deep on the major looming questions surrounding the company. Read more. And if you’re at the meeting, reach out to Brittany to say hi.
Maternity care deserts persist
The March of Dimes released last week its biannual report on maternity care deserts in the U.S. Here are some of the key findings:
- Between January 2024 and May 2026, at least 96 labor and delivery units closed. And in nearly 60% of counties that saw a unit close, it had been the only local birthing facility.
- About 1 in 3 U.S. counties are maternity care deserts, meaning there’s no obstetric clinicians or birthing facilities. The closure of rural hospitals has a major impact on the availability of maternity care. Incoming Medicaid changes could further exacerbate access issues, per the report authors.
- About 1 in 9 reproductive-age women in the country are uninsured, with the worst rates in the South, rural areas, and maternity care deserts.
Some more great STAT stories from last week
There’s nothing like a week off from the newsletter to really demonstrate how much great reporting happens here every day. Sorry to sound so #sponsored, but there are a few more stories from last week that I want to make sure you saw:
- Casey and Brittney published a monthslong investigation into a $7 billion tech startup that uses AI to automate administrative tasks in health care. Their reporting found that the company offers thousands of dollars of compensation to customers and other parties willing to refer its products to new business prospects. Or at least it used to — follow-up reporting revealed that the company has terminated programs that pay partners for referrals.
- A new study suggests there may be no harm in stopping statins at age 75 in people with no history of cardiovascular disease, STAT’s Elizabeth Cooney reports.
- Brain-computer interface startups love to tout their devices as “minimally invasive.” But as STAT’s O. Rose Broderick reports, it’s a slippery term. A new study polled patients considering implantable devices for treatment-resistant depression about what mattered to them.
- Medical ethicists say research oversight has become overly beholden to industry priorities. STAT’s Angus Chen wrote about one nonprofit that its founders believe can save an industry that’s lost its way.

China’s self-driving push gains ground in Europe as Momenta, Pony.ai expand
Deutsche Bank raises its price target for Momenta while Pony.ai widens partnership with Uber to accelerate autonomous-vehicle roll-out in European cities
China’s autonomous-driving ambitions are winning growing recognition in Europe, with Deutsche Bank raising its target price for Momenta following a key regulatory breakthrough, and Pony.ai expanding its European robotaxi roll-out alongside Uber Technologies.
In a research note released on Monday, Deutsche Bank analyst Bin Wang saw Momenta as the “No 1 independent autonomous-driving solution provider globally”, particularly in the urban “navigation on autopilot” (NOA) segment.
“Momenta’s market share in the urban NOA segment is 64.5 per cent,” the analyst said. “It collaborates with nine of the top 10 global automakers and has strategic shareholders including Mercedes-Benz, Toyota and GM.”
The German investment bank has initiated its coverage of the Chinese firm, which raised about HK$5.9 billion (US$752 million) in an initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong a month ago. It set a target price of HK$400 per share, compared with Friday’s closing price of HK$268.40, with a “Buy” rating.
The recognition came as Momenta secured approval to conduct nationwide urban-road testing of Level 4 autonomous-driving systems in Germany last month. Level 4, or “high automation”, is the second-highest level of vehicle automation and is the standard used in commercial robotaxi services. Level 5 would represent “full automation”.
Meanwhile, Chinese autonomous driving firm Pony.ai, backed by Baidu, announced last week a major expansion of its strategic partnership with Uber. Under the plan, Pony.ai will provide Level 4 autonomous-driving technology and operational experience, with more than 2,000 robotaxis to be deployed across five European cities.

Like the pets of any self-respecting millennial, my cats have their own Instagram account.
How to take better photos of your pets
Tips and tricks to get your pet looking their best.
Noodle and Loaf — aka Carb Cats — aren’t exactly celebrities. But they are used to having their photos taken a lot. Between their Instagram account, my regular need to test smartphone cameras, and the fact that they are two adorable idiots, I’ve taken on an unofficial household role as pet photographer.
I know I’m not the only one. It’s become standard practice to maintain a camera roll full of blurry bleps and dozing dogs. But pets are rarely easy to photograph. They’re usually small, fast, and don’t take direction well. Here are a few ways to improve your odds.
The hardware
Most of the photos I take are because one of the cats is doing something cute right now, and so the best camera for the job is the one I have on me. That’s usually my phone, which is how I’ve taken the overwhelming majority of my pet photos, with a handful more shot on film.
A good camera will certainly bring advantages, and I wouldn’t want to put anyone off getting into the hobby. In this case, a better phone camera might be more beneficial though — and is probably cheaper.
If you really do want to make an investment, the best bang for your buck is in lighting. I have a cheap $40 softbox light from Raleno, originally purchased for the sake of taking product photos, but occasionally repurposed with the cats in mind. The extra light helps bring out details and stops indoor shots from looking too flat or too yellow, common issues when you’re reliant on regular household lights. It can be useful for the occasional staged shot (easier with some pets than others), but won’t help much with candids.
The settings
I also mostly shoot in the default camera mode. What can I say? I’m lazy. That may work just fine for you too, but if you want to dive into specific shooting modes or play with settings manually, there are some tweaks worth making.
The big one is shutter speed. Most pets aren’t great at sitting still, and you’re probably used to taking photos that are ruined by motion blur. The quickest fix is a faster shutter speed, which shortens the exposure time to capture sharper shots of moving subjects. Many Android camera apps have a dedicated sports mode, which does this for you — how much difference is there really between a professional athlete and a cat with zoomies?
iPhones don’t have a sports mode, but instead you can try burst mode, which you’ll also find on most Androids. It takes a bunch of photos in quick succession with short shutter speeds, perfect for when you’re trying to catch a dog mid-run or a cat darting after a toy, giving you a selection of action shots to choose from.
The caveat is that shorter shutter speeds mean less light capture. That’s usually fine in bright daylight, but in dimmer lighting — and sometimes even simply if you’re indoors — quality will drop. I took this shot of Noodle trying to grab a toy using burst mode, and it captured her crisply but introduced a whole lot of noise into the black parts of my computer displays behind her.
You might also want to think about aperture. Pet photos are just like any portrait and often benefit from a blurred background that helps draw attention to the subject. Phones can add this bokeh effect through portrait mode, but if you’re tweaking manually, then dropping the aperture will get the right result. Just don’t drop it too far — most pets have deeper faces than humans, and too wide an aperture risks leaving their nose in focus while the ears are blurry. Somewhere between f/4 and f/5.6 is about right; play around to find what works.
Switching to a telephoto lens, whether on a real camera or on your phone, can help a portrait pop a little more, and has the added bonus of letting you shoot from a distance, reducing the odds that you’ll ruin the moment in your attempt to get close. Check if your phone has a dedicated telephoto lens — zooming in on the main camera won’t have the same effect.
Drop to eye level
Hardware and software aside, what about technique?
The single biggest improvement you can make is to get on their level. Don’t shoot your pet from standing; pop a squat and take a photo from head-on, just like you would if you were photographing a person. There’s nothing cuter than capturing big puppy-dog eyes up close.
If that’s tricky for whatever reason, try to snatch photos when your pets are elevated. My cats love to nap in raised radiator beds, and I used to photograph my parents’ Chihuahuas while they slept on the staircase. For reptiles, rodents, and other pets in tanks or cages, this is often easier, though shooting through the glass or bars will have an impact on quality. Take them out of the tank if that’s feasible.
Shots from standing can work, but it’s rare. Your photos look less considered and lower effort, and it’s much harder to frame them against a good backdrop or get that bokeh blur.
Break out the toys and treats
Even a free-spirited pet can be manipulated a little. Treats and toys are the best ways to maneuver most animals into position and control their attention.
Eye contact is one of the easiest ways to upgrade a photo, and for that you need to get your pet looking into the lens. My go-to is shaking a rattly, colorful toy directly above the camera (or asking my partner to do it for me). Cats are tricky because they get bored quickly, so you might need a variety of toys within easy reach to keep their attention.
Direct eye contact can produce brilliant photos, but some of my favorites have the cats looking off at an angle. The key is to make sure you’re still capturing their eyes, whether it’s head-on or not, and that they’re looking roughly toward the brightest light around.
Treat them like a wild animal
One of the classic mistakes is treating pets like kids: a little unpredictable but fundamentally capable of being controlled. Instead, treat them like wild animals.
Don’t go breaking out a pith helmet just yet, but try to photograph them on their own terms. You know when your dog is likely to be sleepy, so get that dozy shot when it’s naptime. If your cat loves to sprawl in sunbeams, wait for the light to get right and let them pose themselves. Noodle and Loaf always get the zoomies at night, so I know that’s when to nab playtime photos. You’ll know your own pets best, so plan around their habits.
My view on this is obviously shaped by owning cats, and before them several badly trained Chihuahuas. If you have a pet that’s better at following instructions, then by all means take advantage.
Either way, you’re guaranteed to take a load of terrible photos. You’ll get blurry ones because they moved too fast. You’ll get derpy ones because they yawned at just the wrong moment. You’ll get more direct shots of their ass than you’re entirely comfortable with.
Accept these facts. Make your peace with the bad shots and the buttholes, because you’ll have to get through them to get the perfect photo. And hey, sometimes the derpy ones end up being your favorites anyway.

I’m already growing hoarse in Golden Gate Park as Charli XCX takes the stage at a San Francisco music festival. The crowd starts jumping as a guitar hook hits, and I reluctantly comply, bouncing around on these aging knees as my chunky Puff necklace almost flies off the chain.
During a lull in the set, someone next to me compliments the necklace, which has stainless steel swirls and a bulbous orange center. Their eyes grow wide as I flip the cap off and explain that it’s a hidden USB flash drive—I plugged the Puff into my phone to show off the animations.
When Harry Isaac and Sebastian Bidegain, working together under the Noware moniker, posted an early prototype of their retro-futuristic necklace on social media in 2025, it quickly racked up over a million views with thousands of waitlist sign-ups to buy one. The duo has spent the last year attempting to turn the online attention on their prototype into a mass-produced reality. Now, Noware is finally ready to ship units this October.
The pair arrived at the WIRED office wearing Puff necklaces, naturally, that match with their trendy gorpcore outfits. They seem nervous, albeit excited, to show off their creation. Neither has had a wide release for their products before, though both are well-versed in whimsical designs. Isaac previously went viral for making an electric scooter that shoots out bubbles. Bidegain was already sculpturally approaching electronics, with prototypes like a vape camera and lo-fi sampler built into a rock.
The design ethos of the Puff is just as much about aesthetics as it is about usefulness. Noware’s marketing materials show a cool girl with a Puff clipped onto her purse, where a Labubu might have sat last year, as well as styled on her neck with a pile of other silver chains. Bidegain says the “squishy, doughy” textures of food partially inspired Puff’s design, as well as cellular biology and tactile devices, like old phones and radios.
“On one end, I want anyone to be able to wear it, just if they think it's pretty,” he says. “Though, I also want people who actually find utility in flash drives as part of their workflow: photographers, DJs, IT people.”
The small screen in the middle of the necklace is my favorite aspect. When it’s plugged into my phone or laptop, Puff’s center lights up with a customizable design. The Noware duo showed me goopy animations that reacted to the direction I held the phone as well as an aquarium mode. They even put the WIRED logo on it through custom software anyone can use to craft their own designs. The Puff doesn’t have an internal battery, so the USB drive can live as a piece of jewelry far longer than the expiration date of most electronics.
The necklace’s biggest drawback is its price: a whopping $179 for only 128 GB of storage. A basic flash drive with similar storage costs around $30. The duo doesn’t want the Puff to remain that expensive and hopes to reach a more accessible price. “We want it to get cheaper over time, but we're just trying to make it exist first,” says Isaac. They blame it partially on the inflated cost of memory right now, thanks to the AI boom. Depending on how Puff’s initial release goes, future iterations may include more budget-friendly options, like a nonmetal version.
This experimental device from two New York City-based makers was the perfect accessory for a weekend-long festival, with its retro-futuristic vibe and sharp colors.
“We're very interested in making electronics that are more opinionated, playful, and personal,” Isaac says. It was a lighthearted conversation piece as I made small talk with vendors, and at least one friend assumed I was hiding drugs in it. (Nope, just a bunch of nudes.)

Historic Visakhapatnam Airport is in the spotlight since it ceased commercial flight operations on 16 August 2026. The last flight to take off from its airstrip was Delhi bound flight 6E 2018 operated by IndiGo, which departed at 10:45 pm on Sunday. The airport is spread over an area of 350.31 acres has a single operational runway. Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh is now serving passengers in place of Vizag Airport, PTI reported. Flight services commenced from the Alluri Sitarama Airport on Monday with the first flight IndiGo arriving from Hyderabad. This was followed by an Air India Express flight from Bengaluru. The IATA airport code ‘VTZ’ also shifted from Visakhapatnam Airport to the Bhogapuram airport from 12:01 am on 17 August. Union Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu marked the beginning of operations at the new international airport almost 16 days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama airport on 1 August. The Aviation Minister flagged off the first commercial flight after handing over boarding passes to passengers. Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu in a statement said, "The commencement of commercial flight operations at Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport is a matter of great happiness and pride. This marks the beginning of a new chapter for North Andhra and will open new opportunities for the region," PTI reported. Visakhapatnam Airport director in a post on X on 10 August stated, “AAI Visakhapatnam Airport notifies to passengers that all flight movements will be commenced at Bhogapuram w.e.f. 17.08.2026 0001 hrs. Kindly note and make your travel arrangements accordingly.” Visakhapatnam Airport Director N Purushottam issued a farewell message for employees, stakeholders and partners and in a press release stated, “Visakhapatnam Airport has reached an important milestone with the conclusion of its scheduled commercial operations, and we sincerely acknowledge the contribution of every employee, stakeholder and partner who supported the airport’s operations and passenger services over the years." Suspension of operations at Visakhapatnam Airport follows the Ministry of Civil Aviation’s notification announcing that scheduled commercial flights at the Visakhapatnam Civil Enclave will cease with the start of operations at Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram at 12.01 am on 17 August. While scheduled commercial operations were transferred to the new airport, Visakhapatnam Airport is now being used under general aviation for private flights. Visakhapatnam Airport's establishment dates back to the Second World War when an airstrip was constructed for the Royal Air Force. The airport briefly opened for civil operations in 1962 before resuming regular flights only in 1976. In December 1972, the Indian Navy commenced aviation operations at this airport. A helipad along with hangars were built adjacent to the airfield in 1976. Indian Navy claimed the ownership of the airport on 12 March 1986 from the Airports Authority of India and the airport was designated as ‘Naval Air Station, Visakhapatnam’. Additional facilities were constructed soon after and on 21 October 1991, the air station was renamed and formally commissioned as INS Dega. In the 21st century, its expansion continued until it suffered extensive damage due to the cyclone Hudhud. After this tragedy, an agreement was signed to move civilian operations from the airport to Bhogapuram. "The deepest sin against the human mind is to believe things without evidence." — Thomas Henry Huxley.
The quote above is attributed to Thomas Henry Huxley (1825-1895), the English biologist often known as “Darwin's bulldog” for his defence of the theory of evolution. The line, appearing in his 1893 Romanes Lecture, Evolution and Ethics, was delivered at Oxford and followed by an observation that “science is simply common sense at best.”
Here, Huxley elevates a familiar principle and transforms it into a moral one. He doesn't say that believing without evidence is a mistake; he further emphasises it by saying that it is a “sin”, the “deepest” one against the human mind at that. For Huxley, the human mind's defining capability is its ability to reason from evidence, and believing without evidence is betraying what makes humans human.
The point isn't that there should be full certainty about everything, but that the strength of belief should be proportional to the evidence for it. Accepting something as true because it is popular or widely accepted is the most grave kind of intellectual failure.
The world we live in circulates information at an unprecedented scale, whether through social media, word of mouth, or traditional media; often, this happens faster than it can be validated or verified. A mind that believes something is true just because it's widely repeated is easily led, and misinformation operates on this concept.
Huxley reminds readers that the responsibility for scrutiny lies within the reader. They should be able to question any claim rather than blindly believe it. Everyone should have the capacity to ask “does this sound right” or “what is the evidence” when choosing to believe a claim.
Taking an extreme stance of refusing to believe anything without evidence can lead to its own kind of paralysis, since much of life relies on reasonable trust. So, Huxley's quote can be taken as a warning against never asking questions to verify a claim, rather than as a rule for life in general.
1. Match belief to evidence
Ideas should only be held as firmly as the evidence warrants.
2. Popularity is not proof
That many people believe something says little, believing in something based on majority belief is what Huxley warns against.
3. Comfort is a warning sign
Be most sceptical of the beliefs you most want to be true. Wishing rarely makes for good evidence.
4. Ask "how do I know this?"
Before repeating a claim, trace it back. Much of what we know turns out to be something we simply absorbed.
5. Scepticism is a discipline, not cynicism
Demanding evidence is not the same as refusing to believe anything. The goal is accurate belief, not endless doubt. After all, a mind that asks for evidence is not being difficult.

Two Indian students have launched Bribes.fyi, a website that allows people to report incidents involving bribery. The platform calls itself a “free, crowdsourced platform” where citizens can share instances in which they were asked to pay a bribe at government offices, including cases where they refused to pay. The website compiles the submissions and categorises them by department, city and state, with the aim of giving the public an overview of reported patterns of corruption. The platform was created by Aryan Nishad, a BTech student at Maharaja Agrasen Institute Of Technology. According to the domain information associated with the website, bribes.fyi is registered with NameCheap Inc. The website was launched on July 2. Based on the website's design and appearance, it appears Nishad may have used AI-assisted “vibe coding” to build the platform. Reports submitted by users are organised on the website into three categories — reports, departments and cities. The platform also enables users to compare reported bribe demands across different government departments. The departments currently listed include the Police, RTO, Revenue/Land Records, Passport Office, Municipal Corporation, GST Office, Electricity Board, Income Tax, and Food and Drug Administration. As of August 17, the website showed 646 reported bribes across 258 cities. It also said that 37% of people who reported being asked for a bribe refused to pay but still managed to get their work done. The Police Department accounts for the highest number of reports on the platform, with 349 cases. The RTO follows with 100 reports, while Revenue/Land Records has 69. The Passport Office has 43 reported cases, followed by Municipal Corporations with 30. Among the states listed on the website, Karnataka has the highest number of reported bribe cases, at 138. Maharashtra follows with 91 reports and Uttar Pradesh with 75. Delhi has recorded 47 reports, while Telangana and Haryana have 37 and 35, respectively. West Bengal has 34 reports, followed by Tamil Nadu with 27. Bihar has 29, and Andhra Pradesh 27. When it comes to the average reported bribe amount, Jammu & Kashmir ranks first at ₹19,067, based on six reports. Chhattisgarh comes next, with an average of ₹13,000 from two reports. Maharashtra ranks third, with an average reported bribe of ₹10,238 across 83 reports. The website's data shows that Assam has the highest refusal rate, at 100%. Quick Summary
Apple Maps uses simple icons for search, directions, map modes, current location, weather, saved places, offline maps, sharing ETA, reporting incidents, and more. This guide explains every symbol and button across the app’s main screens.
Apple Maps has steadily improved over the years, but it still needs to catch up with Google Maps, especially in places like global coverage, public transport options, offline navigation, real-time traffic data, and much more. But if you are using an iPhone, unless you use Google Maps even on iOS, like me, Apple Maps is the default and the best choice for most people.
Apple Maps is cleaner and more properly integrated with the other Apple ecosystems. If you live in a place where Apple Maps goes one-on-one with Google Maps, then you shouldn’t even look further than Apple Maps for your navigation.
However, if you are a beginner or switching to Apple Maps from Google Maps, some icons and features can be confusing at first. Thanks to Apple, which kept the interface simpler, you don’t need an enormous learning curve to know how to use it. Most of the features are easy, and the icons are easily recognizable, but this guide helps you go even further by guiding you to know what every icon and feature means in Apple Maps.
This is a very comprehensive guide. It includes every Apple Maps screen and the meaning of every icon on each screen. You can also bookmark this page. In the future, if you get stuck on any icon you are wondering about, you can simply open this page and get to know what that icon means.
Table of Contents
What Do All the Icons and Symbols in Apple Maps Mean?
Apple Maps Home Screen Icon Meanings
- Map Options: Using this, you can change the Apple Maps options. Currently, Apple Maps supports Driving, Public Transport, Satellite, Explore, and much more. Also, depending on your selection, the map icon changes.
- Recenter Map: When you are navigating, you can recenter your position.
- Profile Menu: Tapping on your profile picture reveals the places you saved, reports, offline maps, your preferences, and much more.
- Voice Search: You can use the voice mode to search for places. This is just a voice mode and not a voice assistant.
- Search Maps: This is the main search bar for the maps where you can search for places, destinations, and much more.
- Compass: Apple Maps also comes with a native compass option that lets you easily find which direction you are pointing to. It only appears when you rotate the map and tap on it, pointing to the north direction.
- Weather & Air Quality: It shows the current temperature and local AQI for any location you are pointing to.
- Current Location: This shows your current location, and it blinks slightly, and the shadow cone is the direction you are pointing to.
Apple Maps Profile Screen
- Profile Menu: This is the same profile icon you see before swiping up for more details.
- Saved Places: Here you can view Home, Work, and saved places.
- Your Guides: Similarly, in this section you can see and open favorites and saved guides.
- Share My Location: A quick button lets you perform various tasks; the Share your current location button allows you to instantly share your current location.
- Mark My Location: This button instantly saves your current location.
- Report an Issue: This helps you report a Maps issue; you can report incidents, route issues, street issues, and much more.
Apple Maps Search Screen
- Search Maps: The main search bar allows you to search for different places with suggestions below.
- Voice Search: Use your voice; this is a speech-to-text converter, not a voice assistant.
- Close Search: You can close the search.
- Find Nearby: These are the default recommendations that all Apple Maps users see.
Apple Maps Place Details Screen
- Share Place: If you are looking at any particular location, you can tap on the share to share it with your friends or family.
- Close Details: Close the details card about this place.
- Download Map: You can save the map offline, but use it if you want to use your maps offline, especially when there is no internet in the place you are visiting.
- Directions: You can get directions to this place; it already shows you the current driving mode and the time to get there.
- Place Information: You can use the key details about the place, including its popular name, elevation, area, and much more.
- Add to Library: You can save this place.
- Add to Favorites: You can mark this place as a favorite.
- More Options: Open more place actions.

- Travel Time: Tapping on the three-dot button also reveals more places along with other information; first, it shows the current driving mode, and also the time to get to that location.
- Add to Places: Next, you can add the place to your favorites. You can simply tap on “Add to Places.”
- Add to Guides: You can also add this place to the guides. For those who are not aware, guides contain multiple places.
- Add a Note: You can add a Note about the place.
- Favorite: You can mark the place as a favorite.
- Pin: You can pin this place.
- Share: You can also share the place by tapping on the three-dot menu and tapping on the share option.
- Report an Issue: Report a problem here, such as the name is wrong, the address or location map is wrong, the hours are wrong, the closed category is wrong, and much more.
Apple Maps Directions Screen
- Driving: This is a part of Apple Maps direction options. Driving includes mostly the car option.
- Walking: Get directions if you want to go on foot.
- Public Transport: If you select this mode, it prioritizes public transport, listing all the available transit options. In some cities, Apple Maps also supports timing and much more.
- Ride: Using this icon, you can find the ride options. Using this icon, you can find the ride options.
- Cycling: It shows cycling directions.
- Starting Point: You can set the trip starting point using this location.
- Destination: You can set the destination using this option.
- Reorder Stops: If you have added any places in between, you can reorder them; you can simply drag their position.
- Voice Input: You can just add a stop using your voice note.
- Add Stop: You can add another stop.
Apple Maps Add Pin Screen
This screen appears when you are trying to pin a new place. You can tap on the add plus option under the places section.
- Confirm Pin: Once you select the location, you can tap on this to confirm and save the location.
- Voice Search: Search the place using the voice note.
- Pin Suggestion: Apple also offers some pin suggestions if you want to.
- Search: You can search for a place and pin it.
- Siri Suggestions: You can view the Siri suggestions based on your past location history and the places you frequently visit.
Apple Maps Navigation Screen
- Current Position: This icon shows your live location.
- Share ETA: It lets you share your estimated arrival time (ETA) with others.
- Trip Details: Shows the arrival time, travel time, distance, and more.
- Navigation Instruction: This icon shows how to take the next route action.
Apple Maps Route Steps Screen
This screen appears if you tap on the route, which displays all your routes.
- Collapse Directions: It hides the turn list.
- Proceed to Route: Guides you back to the route.
Apple Maps Route Options Screen
This screen appears if you swipe up when you are navigating; it reveals more details about your trip.
- Route Stops: Shows stops and arrival times that you have set; you can also add a new stop.
- Add Stop: You can add a new stop.
- Share ETA: Share your arrival time, the same option that appears by default; you can tap on it to select the contacts of friends you want to share the ETA with.
- Report an Incident: You can report a road incident if you see any while you are navigating.
- Voice Controls: You can control the directions and all with your voice, especially useful if you don’t want to see the map while driving and get hands-free voice directions; remember it is not an assistant, it is one-way.
- End Route: Stop the navigation and quit the current navigation.
- Trip Summary: The same quick info that shows the ETA, travel time, and distance even if you swipe up.
Apple Maps Profile Menu Screen
This is the profile screen that appears if you tap on the profile option.
- Profile: This is your Apple Maps profile; it is basically your Apple ID profile that also appears here, listing your name and email.
- Close: You can use these icons to close the profile menu.
- Places: You can view your saved places.
- Reports: Here you can view your submitted reports.
- Offline Maps: You can view and manage all your downloaded offline maps.
- Preferences: You can change and set default Apple Maps preferences. The options include directions mode, driving mode, including the ability to avoid tolls on highways. While you are walking, you can avoid hills and busy roads, prefer specific public transport types, and also access map settings and much more.
Apple Maps Offline Maps Screen
This is the screen that appears when you tap on the offline maps option from the profile screen.
- Download Map: You can start downloading an offline map. You can select your current location or locate specific maps to download offline.
- Offline Maps: You can access all your downloaded offline maps here.
Apple Maps Places Screen
This page appears when you tap on the Places option in your profile screen.
- Pinned: Here you can view pinned places.
- Saved Places: Also view saved locations.
- Guides: Also view and manage your Guides from here.
- Routes: View saved routes.
- Recently Added: Also view all your recently added places.
Apple Maps Reports Screen
This is the screen that appears when you tap on the report option from the profile screen.
- Report a New Issue: Using this button, you can submit a new map issue.
- Report Status: Here you can view your submitted reports.
Apple Maps Preferences Screen
This is the preferences screen that appears when you tap on the preferences screen from the profile screen.
- Preferences: Manage route preferences.
Understanding Apple Maps Icons
These are what the icons mean in Apple Maps. Unlike Google Maps, Apple Maps is a lot simpler and offers a clean and similar experience to other Apple apps. However, Apple keeps adding new features and screens. Because of this, we update this post regularly to keep up with Apple updates. If you find any icon that you are not familiar with, you can also comment below, share the icon details, and we are happy to guide you.

Europe's scorched landscapes seen from space after summer heatwaves
- Published
The impact of this summer's extreme temperatures on western Europe can now be seen from space after successive heatwaves since May.
Satellite images examined by BBC Verify show shrunken glaciers, scorched areas left by wildfires, green fields turned arid and lower river levels.
And some landmarks have been affected, too. The Palace of Versailles, south of the French capital Paris, appears as an island of trees surrounded by brown fields in these images.
The EU's climate monitoring service, Copernicus, has confirmed that western Europe experienced its hottest June-to-July period on record.
The immediate cause of the heatwaves has been persistent high-pressure weather systems bringing clear, sunny skies and allowing temperatures to build, according to the Met Office.
But climate change, mainly due to the burning of fossil fuels, has been raising average temperatures for decades and making hot spells much more likely and intense.
We've taken a look at how the sweltering weather has left its mark on landscapes across the continent.
Rivers run drier
The waters of the Danube, Europe's second-longest river, have dropped to their lowest levels for 30 years in several countries.
This has led to unusual discoveries on the river bed, including the bones of a mammoth in Bulgaria and a sunken WW2 warship in Serbia. You can see the sunken ship has emerged from the deep in the right-hand image below.
And where the river snakes through Hungary and Romania, nuclear power stations have been forced to shut down or run at reduced capacity for some time because of an inability to use river water for cooling.
Meanwhile on the Rhine, some cargo vessels have been left stranded and river cruises have been cancelled.
Retreating glaciers in the Alps
Even the snow-capped peaks of the Alps have not escaped the heat.
Ongoing measurements suggest this summer could become one of the worst ever recorded for melting Alpine glaciers, with more than a month of the season still to go.
After a mild winter, glaciers had less snow cover than usual at the end of April - and an unusually early heatwave the following month accelerated the melting of snow.
This exposed the ice beneath, leaving the glaciers vulnerable to melting faster in subsequent heatwaves.
As you can see below, satellite imagery suggests much of the front of Rhône Glacier in Switzerland has retreated by 50m (160ft) or more since the same time last year.
In a stable climate, glaciers would be expected to remain more or less the same size over the long-term.
Dr Lander van Tricht, glaciologist at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, said in recent years climate change has led to "much less snow in winter and much, much more melt in summer.
"And if we continue this trend, then the future looks very dramatic for the Alps."
Wildfires turn landscapes brown
Wildfires have transformed parts of western Europe this summer, too.
More than 90,000 hectares (900 sq km or 350 sq miles) has burned in France. This is already its worst year on record, according to the European Forest Fire Information System.
The largest fire in Gironde region, where the city of Bordeaux is situated, burnt about 42,000 hectares of land - roughly equivalent in size to the Isle of Wight.
Part of the reason this year has been particularly bad for wildfires is that land has been tinder-dry.
Dr Douglas Kelley of the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology tells us extreme wildfires are becoming "more and more frequent" as climate change is creating ideal conditions, with higher temperatures drying out vegetation and soils faster.
Even zoomed-out satellite imagery of western France shows a striking increase in the browning of land compared to last year.
To assess whether 2026 is unusual we used the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), a measure which uses satellite data to assess how green and healthy vegetation is. Lower readings indicate more sparse or stressed vegetation.
The NDVI this summer came in below a five-year benchmark of 2021 to 2025 across about 70% of France. Close to half the UK and roughly 40% of western Germany showed the same.
Prof Andrew Challinor, from the University of Leeds, said the images were "consistent with widespread water stress", which "does not bode well" given much of Europe's land is covered by crops meaning it could hit the agriculture industry and food production.
In the worst-affected areas, soil moisture is lower than on about 98% of comparable dates in the historical record, according to Prof Luis Samaniego, from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research.
And, he warns, even if rain returns, some of the agricultural damage may already have been done.

Hasan Piker has for years now been both an asset and a liability for Democrats. The Twitch streamer has elevated base-energizing progressives, such as Darializa Avila Chevalier and Zohran Mamdani, in interviews and with endorsements. But he’s also stoked controversy with past anti-Israel commentary and generally caused headaches for establishment Democrats who would rather not see Hasan’s favored candidates get any more oxygen.
Hasan Piker isn’t retreating
The Twitch streamer talks Democratic primaries in Wisconsin and Michigan, and what made the difference for progressives who won.
Why? A familiar concept for these kinds of centrist Democrats: electability.
That concept has been on many left-leaning voters’ minds over the past few weeks, as primaries have put progressive candidates to the test — with very mixed results. Last week, Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate and democratic socialist Francesca Hong lost her primary to establishment favorite David Crowley. Not long before that, though, progressive Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed won his primary against the more mainstream Democratic candidate, Rep. Haley Stevens — albeit by a much smaller margin than many polls predicted.
America, Actually host Astead Herndon caught up with Piker to talk about whether the recent primary results have refined his understanding of how prepared Americans are to vote for democratic socialists, what support for unabashedly progressive candidates tells us about the changing working class in America, and the “pundit brain” problem in the Democratic Party.
Below is an excerpt of Astead’s conversation with Piker, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full show, so listen to America, Actually wherever you get your podcasts or watch it on Vox’s YouTube channel.
The last two weeks have produced mixed results for left-wing candidates: a big win in Michigan and a win this week in Minnesota for Peggy Flanagan, but a loss for Francesca Hong, which was a surprise in Wisconsin.
What have been your takeaways from the last set of results?
I think the ground game is phenomenal. There’s a lot of excitement on the platform. There’s a lot of excitement for the first time for “Change Candidates.” It’s still a good environment to be in if you are a socialist.
The establishment does have a lot of juice still, for sure. And when they can put together a similar strategy to what happened in 2020 against Bernie Sanders with Joe Biden, especially in a place like Wisconsin where Tony Evers is very clearly still a very popular governor, they were able to elevate David Crowley’s campaign, who actually had dropped out and consolidated support behind Sara Rodriguez initially. And he had to drop out because he was only performing at, like, 6 percent.
Yeah, the consolidation was swift, and it was complete. I mean, you’re comparing it to 2020, in which the establishment lined up behind Joe Biden and kind of nixed that Bernie Sanders campaign in the blink of an eye. I imagine you were surprised at the result.
I never underestimate my opponents, whether they be Republicans or whether they be establishment Democrats. You have to always operate as though you’re down 10 points. I don’t believe in the notion that we are going to win easy victories at the end of the day.
There are a lot of powerful interests at play here. There are a lot of people in positions of power that don’t wanna lose their seats. So they’re gonna fight like hell, so we have to also fight like hell. We have to fight extra hard, as a matter of fact, because we’re almost always outspent, right?
I got an alert right before we started talking from the New York Times that said, “A democratic socialist lost in Wisconsin, which shows the movement’s surging wave might crash before rippling out from big cities.” Is that wrong?
Oh, I love that. Look, people are gonna have their opinions. I’ll just say it like this.
Abdul El-Sayed’s one-point victory margin showed that the Democratic socialist-aligned movement or the progressive movement was in tatters. It was obviously a failure. And now, David Crowley’s less-than-one-point victory proves that the centrist bulwark is still here, and that the Democratic socialist movement is dying.
It kind of feels like it’s wish-casting for the most part, from a lot of people who maybe want to go back to the way things used to be. My assessment on this is definitely a little bit different. I think, at the end of the day, these are insurgencies, right? These are insurgent candidacies.
We’re talking about no name recognition for a state legislator that was entirely propped up by local Wisconsin DSA chapters. These people didn’t have a lot of money necessarily, and they were able to defy the odds, and they continued defying the odds all the way until the end.
The idea that the polls showed that Francesca was a clear frontrunner and was running away with this race is utterly irrelevant. Especially if you were to look at this with a broader perspective, like thinking about where Democratic Socialists of America have gotten to in the last two years.
I mean, I remember how I felt in 2024, in the aftermath of the DNC, about where the American socialist movement was as opposed to where it is now. We are clearly a force to be reckoned with, and that’s precisely the reason why a lot of people are paying close attention to what’s going on.
And I’ll say it like this. The fact that the Hong campaign did not have any major progressive national endorsements, and that I was like their top surrogate.
There was no Bernie Sanders endorsement, there was no AOC endorsement. That did make the Hong campaign unique on that front.
I think there were a couple other races that I was also involved in where my candidates lost, right?
I mean, Saikat Chakrabarti was another great example of this as well. It wasn’t a statewide race, and obviously, there’s always clear local differences that play a formative role in how these races turn out.
But we’ve looked back at this data. There are a couple different endorsement trackers out there, and they’ll put my endorsement up there, and they’ll put, like, AOC and Bernie Sanders. And it’s very clear that the best likelihood of success usually comes from a consolidation of national progressive forces, whether it be outside expenditures coming from Justice Democrats or things like that. And with the Francesca Hong campaign, I think it’s a testament to their success. It’s a testament to how popular the platform is in general.
And one thing I will have to stress here is the salience of the electability narrative. I think that’s still a real motivator for a lot of people.
Yeah, I hear that. Both El-Sayed’s campaign and Hong’s campaign did better among middle-class voters — I should say, than the data would tell us, among working-class voters. Considering how central working-class and bottom-up issues are to the DSA message, why has it not produced results that actually get it more working-class votes? Because that does seem to be something we’ve learned over the last three, four weeks.
I think that we have to dramatically reconstruct how we understand what it means to be working-class in this country. I think a lot of people will disagree with what I’m about to say here, but we have to do away with this fantastical notion that the working-class is one specific thing.
I think for the longest time, people have thought about this hardhat-wearing coal miner as the true working class, oftentimes White as well. And the working class is unbelievably diverse in this country, and it’s also a lot more college-educated than people actually give it credit for.
I think partially this is because if you look back to the ‘90s as opposed to right now, yes, if you had a college education, you were upwardly mobile. You were probably a professional managerial class individual that was going to be able to retire at a reasonable age. You were doing fairly well. It was a guarantee for getting a good job, right?
That’s not the case in America any longer. There are a lot more people who have a college degree who are downwardly mobile, who are having a very tough time in the current job market, who do not own a home, and it’s seemingly less likely than before that they will ever be able to own a home.
And that is the actual working class. It’s much broader, right? So we’ve seen in Zohran’s race and in Abdul’s race, there’s this massive group of working-class folks that constantly get cast aside as not being a true representation of the American working class, when I think like, No, that is the true representation.

All Malaysia Airlines pilots pass drug tests following Jakarta arrest
The mandatory screening process was ordered after a Malaysian Airlines pilot was arrested in Indonesia on drug trafficking charges
The mandatory screening process was ordered after a Malaysian Airlines pilot was arrested in Indonesia on drug trafficking charges on July 28.
Authorities found 26kg (57lbs) of the mind-altering drug MDMA in his luggage upon his arrival in Jakarta from Kuala Lumpur.

Over the past few weeks, journalists, independent creators, news organisations, activists and Opposition politicians have been reporting a growing number of Instagram accounts being restricted in India or posts being arbitrarily taken down — many of them concerning the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, the brutal police crackdown that followed, or simply content critical of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government or its policies.
While the police arrested and detained protesters across cities, the government has simultaneously been taking down content on Instagram through notices that may have been issued under Section 79(3)(b) or Section 69A of the Information Technology (IT) Act. Yes, may have been, because there is no clarity to the entire mechanism whatsoever.
The Timing of the Censorship Frenzy
The timing of this state-sanctioned censorship frenzy is particularly alarming. It comes in the immediate aftermath of the CJP protests, a youth-led movement whose reach and mobilisation were powered overwhelmingly by the digital ecosystem, particularly Instagram. The platform played a pivotal role in transforming CJP from a satire page into a nationwide movement that forced the government to concede to some of its core demands.
Born as a reaction to a snide remark made by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, CJP found its nucleus in the social media spaces occupied by young people. The group created its Instagram page in early May, posting reels, memes and explainers and rapidly amassing a following that surpassed that of every major political party in India. With 26.5 million followers as of today, CJP demonstrated how online engagement could be converted into massive street mobilisation across the country.
From the 36-day sit-in and hunger strike by Sonam Wangchuk and protesting students, to the Jantar Mantar ‘Sansad Chalo’ march on July 20 and solidarity protests across cities, Instagram was the primary platform through which participants and the wider public received and disseminated information. It enabled volunteers, creators and ordinary users to amplify protest calls, coordinate demonstrations and broadcast events in real time.
Instagram, owned by Meta, was therefore not merely a digital record of the movement; it was one of the principal engines of it. The scale of the street mobilisation, catalysed by the platform, eventually forced the government to concede to several of CJP’s core demands, including former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation, compensation for families of students who died by suicide, and several reformative measures announced by the government.
It is against this backdrop that the timing of the current censorship becomes especially significant. A platform that proved capable of turning youth discontent into one of the country’s largest grassroots movements is now at the centre of an opaque censorship drive, raising questions about what and who the state is seeking to silence.
Anti-establishment Wave Forces Modi to Make Reels
This digital upheaval also managed to create an unprecedented anti-establishment wave, which not only led to the resignation of a cabinet minister for the first time in BJP’s 12-year rule but also compelled Prime Minister Narendra Modi to create Instagram reels responding to the growing discontentment towards his governance.
The 75-year-old PM, who has not held a single press conference in 12 years, made five consecutive reels wherein he directly addressed the youth protesters — referring to them as ‘friends’ as opposed to his usual ‘Mitron’. A marked departure from BJP’s traditionally scripted social media communication, in his candidly-shot selfie videos, Modi assured the disgruntled Gen-Zs who steered the protest, that his government is committed to taking action against the paper leaks and is actively taking measures to resolve their grievances.
The entire censorship drive is playing out concurrently with tensions deepening between Meta and the BJP government, with many suspecting that the rise in censorship of anti-government content on Instagram is a result of the former succumbing to pressure.
The tech giant drew the government’s ire after it claimed to have erroneously removed Modi’s July 23 post addressing the protesting students from Facebook. Although the video was quickly restored, a parliamentary standing committee gave a three-day ultimatum to CEO Mark Zuckerberg to issue an apology while threatening to revoke the platform’s safe harbour immunity in India. This led to Meta’s chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan reportedly flying in from the United States, meeting Union minister Ashwini Vaishnav and apologising on behalf of the company on Wednesday.
‘Blanket Ban On Protest, Modi Related Content’
However, Modi’s ‘friendly assurances’ did not keep the government from suppressing dissenting voices on Instagram. On August 6, Thursday, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das shared screenshots on X of his Instagram posts being taken down, calling it a “blanket ban on protest and Modi related content”. The two posts, uploaded on June 12 and 18, were about Das’ arrival in Bengaluru for a peaceful protest and CJP securing police clearance for the July 20 protest in Delhi, respectively.

‘Automated’ Crackdown
Two videos uploaded by independent news outlet Maktoob Media on July 21 and 23 were blocked in India under the IT Rules. “Your post is unavailable in India. We restricted access to this content through an automated system implemented pursuant to legal requirements under India’s Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules,” the notification read.
View this post on Instagram
Speaking to Alt News, Maktoob Media editor Aslah Kayyalakkath said, “Both the videos were our original journalistic content analysing the protest and the subsequent police crackdown. Vague Legal Orders and a Dead-end Appeals Process
This lack of transparency and any effective avenue for appeal against the takedowns trap users in a black box of opacity and confusion.
On August 6, the Union ministry of electronics & IT (MeitY) reiterated in a circular that the “timeline for the removal of unlawful content has been reduced from 36 hours to 3 hours”. The circular defines ‘unlawful content’ as “information prohibited under any law for the time being in force in relation to the interest of the sovereignty and integrity of India; security of the State; friendly relations with foreign States; public order; decency or morality; in relation to contempt of court; defamation; incitement an offence relating to the above; or any information which is prohibited under any law…” It is important to note that the amendments were notified as early as February, prior to the CJP protests.
The circular mandates ‘takedown notices’: “Social media intermediaries are required to remove any unlawful information as and when brought to their knowledge either through a court order or through a reasoned intimation, in writing from the Appropriate Government or its agency.” It also outlines a grievance redressal mechanism: “Intermediaries are required to appoint Grievance Officers and resolve complaints within the prescribed timelines. Users can appeal online at https://www.gac.gov.in if their complaints are not addressed by the intermediaries’ Grievance Officers.”
However, in several cases examined by Alt News, users highlighted that they received no prior notice or specific explanation for the restrictions. Meta’s notifications cited only two reasons: restriction in compliance with a legal request and through an automated system based on legal requirements under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act. In most cases, users flagged how these notices were largely vague and lacked any real information on who ordered the restriction or what content allegedly violated the law. They also highlighted lack of an option to appeal for restoration of their accounts or posts, or response on mails sent to Meta directly.
Users said that upon clicking on the ‘See why’ after a post or account is restricted, the same message on automated systems and legal requirements under IT Rules appear and upon clicking ‘Where this happened’, ‘India’ appears as the location where the content is restricted. For ‘How we made this decision’, the exact same message that appeared in the initial notice, “We have taken this action based on a local legal requirement”, reappears; a very similar message is displayed upon opening Meta’s ‘Transparency Centre’ — creating a loop of opaque explanations. Below are the series of messages users encounter:
Affected users also the questioned the ‘automated system’ and and the lack of clarity over how it functions. “What is particularly shocking is Meta’s explanation. What exactly is this automated system? Does this mean there is now a system that automatically identifies and blocks journalistic content in the name of complying with legal requirements? The idea that this process could now be automated, without any transparency about why a particular piece of journalism is being blocked, is deeply alarming and dangerous for press freedom,” said Kayyalakkath.
As public discourse increasingly shifts from the streets to social media feeds, the rise in Instagram censorship begs the question: will there ever remain a space for democratic dissent in this country — online or offline?

“Please don’t let this be the final whistle for Jamshedpur FC,” the defender Pratik Chaudhari said, looking into the camera as teammates looked on disconsolately. “We would like to say on behalf of all the players, please do rethink about this. Because if this happens, this is not just a loss for Indian football … this is a big loss for all of India.”
In addition, fans of the Indian Super League club marched in protest, petitions were launched, and the Indian football legend Sunil Chhetri said it was a “punch to the gut” and joined others in begging for a rethink.
The target of all these pleas was the Jamshedpur owner Tata Steel, which surprisingly pulled the plug on the club on 31 July. After the problems of the 2025-26 campaign, which started five months late and lasted just 13 games, the new season’s big kick-off on 4 September was to be a new start. The positivity and optimism before the new season, fragile though it was, disappeared along with JFC.
And understandably so as it is a huge blow, for players, staff and fans but also for the league. Jamshedpur had solid support and won the ISL shield in 2022, five years after the club was formed. Steve Coppell was the first head coach with Scott Cooper, Aidy Boothroyd and Owen Coyle all following in his footsteps.
Baljit Rihal of Inventive Sports was the agent who took Coppell to the city in the eastern state of Jharkhand. “To be quite frank, after all the uncertainty Indian football has faced over the last couple of seasons, Jamshedpur FC would have been one of the last clubs I expected to pull out,” he told the Guardian.
The club was founded by the Tata Group, which has been involved with Indian football at various levels for decades. “When an institution with that history decides it can no longer continue at the highest level, it says something very serious about the current state of the game,” Rihal said.
The league is also losing a major corporate backer, one which insists, however, that the decision is not about money. “At Tata Steel, sports have never been evaluated through a profit-and-loss lens,” the company’s vice-president and the club’s chairman, Sundara Ramam, told the Guardian.
“Our decision to exit professional club football has nothing to do with Tata Steel’s financial position. In fact, the resources that would have been spent on the club will continue to be invested in grassroots sports development. Our sports budget is not decreasing. It will continue to grow. As chairman of Jamshedpur FC, I can say clearly that this decision was driven by our desire to focus more intensely on grassroots development and not by financial considerations.”
Yet if others follow suit then there may not be much of a professional pathway for young talent. This latest episode shines a light on the league once more. In the club’s original letter sent to the All India Football Federation, concerns were expressed about the financial model of the ISL, which recently changed. Reliance Industries was the federation’s commercial partner from 2010 but, when that agreement expired in 2025, a new deal was not made and a new partner not found, hence the shortened season.
This time, the AIFF looks after governance and administration with the clubs taking on the commercial and marketing side. “The old model meant clubs had very little say in how the league was packaged and sold,” Ravi Puskur, the chief executive of Goa FC, said last month.
“Now the clubs hold the broadcast and sponsorship rights directly. It puts the incentive to grow the league’s commercial value in the hands of the people who are most invested in it growing.”
A member of Jamshedpur’s staff told the Guardian that the decision was because of concerns over the new arrangements. “I believe Tata are not interested in the club-led model,” he says. “There had to be a commitment of four years and the AIFF was asking for an initial payment of around £43,000 from all 14 clubs to be made by 31 July. Tata might have thought it’s better to stop rather than get dragged into unknown waters.”
It is a worrying exit as this is not the only corporate departure from Indian football of late. “Reliance stepping away from its central role was significant,” Rihal says. “City Football Group leaving Mumbai City was another warning.” That happened in December, in the middle of the problems last season. “Tata now withdrawing from Jamshedpur FC feels different again because of the group’s deep-rooted history in Indian football. These departures have happened for different reasons, but collectively they represent a major loss of confidence in the professional game.”
Now there is fear that others may follow and there will be some relief if all 13 remaining clubs kick off the season. “Indian football can recover, but we should not underestimate the scale of the challenge,” Rihal says.
“The priority now must be the people affected, followed by urgent clarity over the league’s structure and future. Players, staff and supporters cannot continue living from one period of uncertainty to the next. They deserve much better.”
There is still hope that Tata could have a rethink. “I understand that some tough decisions in sport are down to what makes sense in the boardroom,” Chhetri said. “But I can only request and hope that the thinktank at Tata picks their heart over head and reconsiders this call. It might be a poor business decision, but it will be the one Indian football needs the most at this hour.”

You can customize websites without coding by using AI to create Tampermonkey user scripts or custom browser extensions. These tools can change fonts, remove clutter, tweak layouts, add features, and apply your changes automatically whenever you visit a site.
We are in the era of personal software. Thanks to AI, anyone can now build fully functional tools as good as existing high-end software for their workflows.

Website owners should spend extra time tweaking to meet user needs.
Many websites that I personally follow and read have used AI to revamp their existing user interface, resulting in the same issues.
Fortunately, I found a way to easily customize website designs once the webpage is rendered. All changes I made to any website are temporary and can be easily reverted.
There are plenty of ways you can tweak website design; however, using extensions and user scripts are two best reliable ways. Those changes will auto-apply every time you visit the webpage.
In this guide, I am going to show you both methods, with step-by-step guides on how to tweak the design of any website.
How to Redesign and Personalize Any Website Without Coding
Just a heads-up: this might not work for every website. Some websites use hard-coded elements that are impossible to tweak, while others use completely different structures where you will need to try various approaches to get what you want without breaking anything.
Method 1: Customize Websites Using Tampermonkey User Scripts
The first method is using user scripts. You can run simple code snippets on your browser console once the web page is rendered. Since these user scripts only work once the website is fully rendered and stored locally on your device, once you refresh the page, everything goes back to normal. But to keep the changes permanently, you can use the Tampermonkey extension, which allows you to run multiple user scripts on any web page and every time you visit the site.
Tampermonkey is free to use. And since all the changes apply locally, you don’t need to worry about breaking everything. Even if it breaks, you can simply disable the added code.
You need to create a script that works for the specific site with all possible changes you want. I recommend using AI tools.
The best approach is to use an IDE where these AI models can directly inspect the website and analyze all the code. Alternatively, you can copy-paste the entire website HTML or the rendered code into any AI chat tool, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, and ask it to generate a user script.

Step 3: Next, you can tap on the extensions icon in the top toolbar and tap on the pin icon next to the Tampermonkey extension.
Step 4: Now tap on Tampermonkey and tap on the plus icon.
Step 5: From here, you can paste the user script that you have generated,
Step 6: Tap on the file option and tap on save.
Step 7: Now, the changes should be automatically applied to your browser. If not, you can tap on Tampermonkey again and click “Run Script” if it is not working by default.
